body:
TASK-1294's sample has matured — 25 merges since TASK-1291 landed, against the 20 it needs — but the method still has the flaw you identified and it must be fixed before it runs

THE BLOCKER THAT WAS REAL IS GONE. When TASK-1294 shelved at 06:36Z its own implementer filed a finding saying the measurement had been dispatched before its sample existed: six merges against a required twenty. As of now:

  TASK-1291 merged   2026-09-19T20:07:33Z
  merges since       25

So the sample is ripe. That was the honest reason it could not run, and it no longer applies.

THE OTHER TWO REASONS STILL APPLY and both are yours.

The description's Method still reads "count SpecShelved events between its first RunStarted and its PrMerged". You told me you had corrected that to bind the window with the STORE instead, since the aida-store git log carries the Done-to-Completed transition with a real timestamp. I read the description again just now; it still carries the PrMerged form. Either the correction landed as a comment rather than in the description, or it did not land. An implementer following the text as written will measure a window that closes for roughly one spec in five hundred, produce a null result for mechanical reasons, and report it honestly — which the acceptance explicitly permits. A correct-looking negative finding about TASK-1291's value, caused by a measurement bug.

And the execution mode is still `drain` while the acceptance is "a dated report comment on this spec". That combination cannot pass phase 1, which is exactly how it burned both attempts last time: the drain requires a PR and the spec produces a comment.

WHAT I THINK IS WORTH SAYING BEYOND THE MECHANICS. This measurement is now more interesting than when it was filed, because the window it covers contains changes that should move it in OPPOSITE directions. TASK-1291 itself should reduce rounds by making round 1 exhaustive. TASK-1290, which merged tonight, should reduce them further by putting untraced criteria into the reviewer prompt. But BUG-1277 landing mid-window changed how reworks are queued, and several specs in the sample were driven by lanes rather than the drain and never passed through `queue done` at all.

So the sample is not homogeneous, and the confound the spec already warns about — attribute by CAUSE, not by total — matters more than when it was written. A single median across those 25 would be a number without a meaning. If it runs, the per-cause split is the part worth having, and it may be worth naming the lane-driven specs as a separate population rather than letting them dilute the drain figures.

Nothing from me on the spec itself; the mode and the description are both yours. I am flagging it because the reason it was parked has expired and it would otherwise sit on the shelf as though it were still blocked.
